Example: 
                    Simplifying Fractions with Unlike Denominators
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
We combine the like terms by adding the coefficients.

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{2}u+\frac{7}{8}u & = \\ (-\frac{1}{2}+\frac{7}{8})u & \end{aligned}
$$

In order to add the coefficients, we have to convert them to have the same denominator.

$$
\begin{aligned}(-\frac{1}{2}+\frac{7}{8})u & = \\ (-\frac{4}{8}+\frac{7}{8})u & = \\ (\frac{-4+7}{8})u & = \\ \frac{3}{8}u & \end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the expression simplifies to $\dfrac{3}{8}u.$

tutorials.name: Introduction
tutorials.problem:
Suppose that we want to simplify the following expression: 

$$
2+\dfrac{5}{2}x -5 + \dfrac{7}{2}x.
$$

  

We begin by collecting like terms.

$$
\begin{aligned}(\frac{5}{2}x+\frac{7}{2}x)+(2-5)\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we combine the like terms, simplifying the coefficients as much as possible.

$$
\begin{aligned}(\frac{5}{2}x+\frac{7}{2}x)+(2-5) & = \\ (\frac{5+7}{2})x+(-3) & = \\ \frac{12}{2}x-3 & = \\ 6x-3 & .\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the simplified expression is $6x-3.$
